blocks.text: Jenny had moved the operations chair closer to the radio.
From there, she could reach the wall map without crossing the room. Seth noticed it when he came in, but said nothing. He put the water glasses on the desk and sat beside her.
Flaming Head hovered above the clear end of the windowsill. His little flame had not grown overnight.
Billy was checking the address of the hospital when the radio interrupted him.
A jewelry store. Two men breaking display cases. A caller had seen a dark green car in the delivery lane behind the shops.
Jenny put down her glass.
“That’s just past the corner,” she said.

Billy traced the block with his pencil. The delivery lane ran behind the row of stores, from the western corner to an exit at the east. A narrow foot passage beside the jeweler cut directly through to that exit.
“Jenny, the west end. See whether the car’s still there. Seth, take the passage. You’ll reach the other end before we could go around.”
Seth leaned over the map.
blocks.alt: Billy marks the delivery-lane exits on a map while Zerdo, Pink Blur, Fist and diminished Flaming Head prepare their response to a jewelry-store robbery.

blocks.text: “There’s a dumpster by that exit. I’ve seen it.”
“If you can close the gap before they reach you,” Billy said. “If you can’t, stand clear.”
Fist rose beside his shoulder.
“And us?”
“The shop. Find out who needs help.”
Jenny looked toward the window.
“We’ll stay together,” she told Flaming Head.
“Watch the corners.” The warning reached her and Seth.
Seth repeated it for the others. Then they left.
The jeweler’s door stood open. A woman behind the counter held a telephone receiver in one hand and pressed the other against her chest.
“They went out the side,” she called. “Two of them. One had a bag.”
Billy went inside. Fist followed him above the broken glass.
Seth took the foot passage beside the shop. It was barely wide enough for two people to pass. He turned sideways around a stack of empty crates and came out beside the lane’s eastern exit.
The dumpster stood against the brick wall where he remembered it. Its open lid showed wet timber, broken plaster and strips of old flooring. Four small iron wheels held it above the pavement.
He looked west.
The green car was still at the far end. One man pulled its passenger door shut. The engine rose in a rough burst.
Seth put both hands against the dumpster’s side.
Jenny reached the western corner as the car began moving.
For an instant she saw the driver through the open side window. He saw her too. His head jerked forward and the car gathered speed.
She followed it into the lane.
Her boots struck the uneven pavement. She stretched her stride, waiting for the familiar rush that used to carry her past moving cars before their drivers could turn their heads.
The rear bumper drew away.
blocks.alt: Pink Blur runs in side profile after the dark green getaway car, falling behind despite her effort.

blocks.text: Farther ahead, the passenger twisted around to look through the back window.
“Stop!”
He turned forward again.
At the lane’s far end, Seth was beside the dumpster.
The first push turned two of the dumpster’s wheels.
Seth shifted his boots and pushed again. The steel container rolled a few inches away from the wall, scraping grit ahead of its casters.
He needed several feet.
He pressed his shoulder to the steel and drove with his legs.
The dumpster moved another hand’s width.
He could hear the car now.
Once he could have lifted the whole thing. Now he could barely keep it moving.
The car was halfway down the lane.
The gap was still much too wide.
He pushed once more.
The driver braked, saw the gap and aimed for it.
blocks.alt: Zerdo strains against a heavy wheeled dumpster while the getaway car passes through the gap and Pink Blur approaches from behind.

blocks.text: Seth let go and stepped back into the foot passage.
The green fender swept past the dumpster. The passenger clutched a dark bag against his knees. Neither man looked at Seth.
At the exit, the driver turned sharply.
A bicycle bell rang twice.
Then came the scrape of metal and a cry.
Seth reached the sidewalk as the cyclist fell beside his overturned bicycle. A small delivery basket had broken loose from the front wheel. Paper-wrapped sandwiches scattered across the pavement.
The green car straightened in the street and accelerated away.
Jenny came out of the lane behind Seth. She took two steps toward the corner, then stopped at the sight of the man on the ground.
Seth was already kneeling beside him.
“Don’t try to get up yet.”
The cyclist’s trouser knee was torn. He held his wrist against his stomach and stared at the basket.
“I didn’t see them coming.”
“Neither did they look,” Jenny said.
She crouched where he could see her.
“What’s your name?”
“Frank.”
“All right, Frank. Where does it hurt?”
He showed her his wrist without letting her touch it.
Across the street, a woman opened a bakery door.
“Call an ambulance, please,” Jenny said. “Tell them a cyclist’s been struck at the delivery-lane exit.”
The woman disappeared inside.
Seth moved the bicycle out of the narrow pedestrian route, then returned to Frank. He kept looking toward the corner where the car had gone.
Jenny saw him do it.
“I couldn’t catch them,” she said quietly.
“I couldn’t move it.”
Frank looked from one to the other.
blocks.alt: Zerdo and Pink Blur stay beside the injured delivery cyclist and overturned bicycle while the green getaway car recedes.

blocks.text: “Can you stay till somebody comes?”
Seth settled beside him.
“Yes.”
By the time the first officer reached the store, Billy had the clerk sitting behind the undamaged counter. Fist hovered nearby, watching the open door.
The broken cases were empty in long patches where trays had been pulled out. The clerk had a shallow cut on one hand. Billy had brought her a clean cloth from the back room.
“Two men,” he told the officer. “Dark green four-door. She saw it parked behind the shop before they came in.”
He opened his notebook.
“The plate began with K and seven. She’s sure of those. The rest she couldn’t see.”
The officer passed the description over his radio.
When another officer took over inside, Billy went to the lane exit. Fist stayed with the clerk.
Jenny was beside Frank. Seth stood a few steps away, directing people around the bicycle.
Billy looked down the clear street, then at the dumpster projecting only a little from the wall.
“Which way?”
Seth pointed.
Billy gave the direction to the officer following him. Then he crouched beside Frank and asked whether anyone had called for help.
The bakery woman came out again.
“They’re on their way.”
At the facility, Jenny laid the empty water glasses in the sink.
Flaming Head drifted from the window toward the table. Seth told him about the shop, the lane and the bicycle. Billy added what the clerk had seen, and Seth passed that on too.
Fist settled level with the tabletop.
“The clerk’s husband came,” he said. “She didn’t want to be alone in there.”
“Good thing you stayed,” Jenny said.
He tipped his red cuff a little, showing its white panel.
Billy spread the street map on the table.
“We knew the exits. We got to both ends.”
Jenny rested her hands on the back of a chair.
“And they still went past us.”
Seth looked at the route Billy had marked. The whole lane fit beneath one finger.
Flaming Head lowered himself until his small light touched the paper.
“You came back when someone needed you.”
Seth repeated the words. Billy glanced at the little flame, then at Jenny.
“Yes,” he said. “We did.”
Nobody put the map away.
The next morning, Daniel Orkleson stopped turning the newspaper halfway through the city pages.
ROBBERS OUTRUN DEFENDERS

Beneath the headline, the account described the jewelry-store theft, a green car and the cyclist taken to the hospital. The driver had escaped through a lane where Super Zerdo had tried to block the exit. Pink Blur had pursued on foot and fallen behind.
A witness outside the shop said she had never seen either hero struggle like that before.
Daniel read that part again.
His shirtsleeves were rolled above his elbows. A brown stain from the ruined collector still marked one cuff. Around him, the relocated workshop stood quiet in the morning light.
He folded the paper back to keep the report uppermost.
On the bench beyond it lay the Army ray, untouched by the rooftop explosion. Farther back, the tank stood beneath the high windows.
Daniel took off his glasses, polished one lens and put them on again.
Then he drew the newspaper closer.
blocks.alt: In shirtsleeves at the relocated workshop, Dork reads a newspaper headed Robbers Outrun Defenders; the intact Army ray and stolen tank remain nearby.
